drills.title: Find every order id
drills.prompt: Arrange the lines into a program that prints every order id (ORD followed by digits) found in a message. The two imports can go in either order. Two lines do not belong.
lines: String text = "Orders ORD1001 and ORD1002 shipped";
drills.explain: In a Java string every regex backslash is doubled: "\\d" reaches the regex engine as \d. A single \d is an illegal escape and does not compile. find() looks for the next match anywhere in the text, so the loop prints both ids, while matches() asks whether the whole text is one match, which is false here, so the loop would print nothing.

drills.title: Groups, validation and replacing
drills.prompt: Fill the blanks so the program pulls the year and month out of an order line, checks a PIN code and masks the digits. Match the goal output.
code: String text = "Order ORD1001 on 2026-11-03 for Rs. 899";
drills.explain: The date sits in the middle of the text, so find() (somewhere inside) is the right call. matches() and lookingAt() need the pattern to cover the whole text or start at the beginning, so they would be false here. String.matches validates a whole value, which is what a PIN code check needs. replaceAll treats its first argument as a regex and replaces every match; replace takes literal text, and replaceFirst stops after one.

drills.title: Nothing changes in place
drills.prompt: Read the code and type exactly what it prints, one line per line of output.
drills.explain: String methods never change the text: toUpperCase returns a new String, and the call on line 4 throws it away, so name is still chai. List.of builds an unmodifiable list, so add throws UnsupportedOperationException. new ArrayList<>(menu) is a separate, changeable copy: it grows to 3 while menu stays at 2.

drills.title: The tag that swallowed everything
drills.prompt: The program should print only the first tag, <b>, but it prints much more. Click the faulty line, then choose the fix.
drills.explain: + and * are greedy: .+ takes as many characters as it can and then backs off only until the last > fits, so the match runs from the first < to the last >. A ? after the quantifier makes it lazy, so it stops at the first >. <.*> is just as greedy, and a ? after the > only makes that final > optional.

drills.title: Review the AI's contact helpers
drills.prompt: An AI assistant wrote these helpers. They compile and run, but tick the real problems (there are three).

issues.text: Pattern.compile is called again for every line
issues.why: Compiling a regex is the expensive part, and the pattern never changes. Build it once, for example private static final Pattern EMAIL = Pattern.compile(...), and call EMAIL.matcher(line) in the loop.

issues.text: f and p say nothing, and 1.18 is a magic number
issues.why: A reader cannot tell that this adds 18% GST. Name the method priceWithGst, the parameter price and the rate a constant (GST_RATE), so a rate change happens in one place.

issues.text: Basket claims to be unchangeable but keeps the caller's list and hands it out again
issues.why: final fields only fix the reference. main adds ravi@shop.in to lines after building the basket, and the basket sees it. Store List.copyOf(items) in the constructor and return the copy (or keep it unmodifiable).

non_issues.text: The backslashes in the pattern are doubled, which looks like a typo
non_issues.why: Inside a Java string \\w is needed to give the regex engine \w. A single backslash would be an illegal escape.

non_issues.text: The loop should use matches() instead of find()
non_issues.why: matches() only succeeds when the whole line is one email. find() locates each email inside the line, which is what the method wants.

non_issues.text: Basket should not be declared final
non_issues.why: final class stops subclasses from adding mutable behaviour, which supports immutability.

drills.explain: In helper code look for work repeated in a loop that could be done once, names and numbers that hide meaning, and classes that call themselves immutable without copying what they receive and return.
